findings.description: Critical: MCP HTTP `claim_immediately` submit and `complete_work` still use different identities, so atomically claimed rows cannot be completed on that transport. `proxy_submit_work` omits body identity and `/work/submit` claims as `resolve_identity(principal, None, None)` (bound principal, else `cloud-agent`). `proxy_complete_work` always injects `**_agent_identity()`, which sends ambient `AGENT_ID` or the proxy default `claude-code-1`. Under an unbound key that yields claim=`cloud-agent` and complete=`claude-code-1`/`AGENT_ID`; under a bound key whose id differs from ambient `AGENT_ID`, complete 403s. Direct/stdio MCP is consistent (`get_config().agent` on both sides), and the dispatcher bridge path correctly completes with `agent_id=None`, but the HTTP MCP surface that this round explicitly forwards `claim_immediately` through remains broken for the paired complete. Ledger failure ordering on the bridge/dispatcher path is otherwise sound: open-before-launch, terminal paths attempt `complete_work` before return, and succeeded findings are withheld when completion fails.
findings.resolution: Make HTTP MCP completion use the same authenticated-principal rule as atomic submit and the bridge: omit ambient identity from `proxy_complete_work` (or take an explicit omit/`agent_id=None` path for claim_immediately rows) so `/work/complete` resolves `resolve_identity(principal, None, None)`. Add a proxy/MCP test that submits with `claim_immediately=True` then completes through `proxy_complete_work` under unbound and bound keys with `AGENT_ID` set, asserting both payloads leave ownership to the server principal.
findings.existing_code:
async def proxy_complete_work(
    task_id: str,
    success: bool,
    result: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    error_message: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Proxy complete_work to POST /work/complete."""
    body = {
        **_agent_identity(),
        "task_id": task_id,
        "success": success,
        "result": result,
        "error_message": error_message,
    }

findings.description: none: Round-2 remediations are present in the worktree and `/tmp/dg02-round3.patch`: dispatcher `_complete_completion_ledger` passes `agent_id=None` (no ambient `AGENT_ID`); `claim_immediately` is omitted by default and forwarded only when true through bridge, HTTP proxy, and direct/HTTP MCP submit; migration is uniquely `043_atomic_submit_claim.sql` with `SECURITY INVOKER`, pinned `search_path`, reserved projection-key rejection, `REVOKE`/`GRANT` to `service_role` only; succeeded `result={}` is passed through unchanged and fails closed; async logs/manifest retain `vendor_task_id`/`task_id`/`ledger_task_id`/`async_dispatch`; separate `ledger_claimer`/`try_get_work` claim interface is removed. Remaining blocker is finding #1 on MCP HTTP complete identity.
findings.resolution: Keep the landed remediations; fix finding #1 before treating HTTP MCP `claim_immediately` as a complete lifecycle.
